rounds.text: Venus Remedies is fundamentally undervalued, trading at a modest P/E of 18.4 [E1] while delivering explosive recent growth, including a trailing twelve-month profit surge of 149% [E21] and a 20% jump in TTM sales [E17]. Profitability metrics easily outpace sector benchmarks, with a robust ROCE of 19.85% versus the sector's 11.68% [E10] and an ROA of 13.61% compared to a 5.78% sector average [E8]. Operating margins have also expanded significantly by 10 percentage points over three years to reach 20% in the TTM period [E30]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt-free with a negligible debt-to-equity ratio of 0.02x [E38] and boasts stellar cash generation, recording an operating cash flow of Rs 156 Cr that fully backs reported profits at a 1.51x cash conversion rate [E34]. A discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 3532 per share, offering a substantial margin of safety of 54.7% [E46, E47], supported by a high-confidence rules-based screen score of 95 out of 100 [E65]. Conceded: [E63, E64].

The fundamental growth profile of Venus Remedies Ltd contradicts its recent price expansion, marked by a pedestrian 7% compounded sales growth over both 10-year and 5-year periods [E14, E15]. This top-line stagnation coincides with an inconsistent yearly operating margin trend over the last three years [E32], while historical profitability has also proved lackluster with a 10-year median return on equity of just 5% and a low 3-year average of 10.5% [E26, E64]. Market expectations have raced ahead of actual delivery, as recently evidenced by price growth outpacing profit growth by 103% alongside negative institutional money flow and a holding change reduction of 0.19 percentage points [E45, E58]. Furthermore, the equity carries severe structural tail-risks defined by extreme annualised volatility of 97.9% and a brutal historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -95.5% [E54, E55]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong recent momentum with TTM profit growth of 149%, an operating margin expansion to 20%, and a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.02x [E21, E30, E38].

Conceded: the 10-year and 5-year compounded sales growth is 7% [E14, E15], but this long-term view ignores a sharp acceleration to 12% over 3 years and 20% over the trailing twelve months [E16, E17], driven by a robust rules-based screen score of 95 out of 100 [E65]. While the 10-year median ROE was low at 5% [E26], recent profitability has surged to a 17% median ROE over the last year [E29] alongside an operating margin expansion to 20% in the TTM [E30], proving that past stagnation has given way to powerful margin and earnings leverage. Conceded: institutional money flow shows a slight negative reading of -0.19 percentage points [E45], yet foreign and domestic institutions have both expanded their overall stakes since September 2023 [E43, E44], and price expansion is fully justified by fundamental delivery where trailing profit growth reached 149% [E21] and net profit jumped 130% year-over-year [E68]. Conceded: the historical drawdown is severe at -95.5% [E54], but the company is now conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.02x [E38] and is backed by exceptional cash generation where operating cash flow fully covers reported profit at 1.51x [E34]. Finally, the inconsistent yearly margin trend [E32] is countered by strong recent quarterly results showing operating margins at 19% in June 2026, up 8 percentage points from the year-ago quarter [E31].

While the Bull highlights a recent 20% sales spike [E17], the long-term 5-year and 10-year compounded sales growth remains a poor 7% [E14, E15, E63], suggesting recent performance may be an outlier rather than a structural shift. Although recent margins and ROE have improved [E29, E30], the yearly operating-margin trend is officially inconsistent over the last three years [E32], and the median return on equity over the last three years is a low 10% [E28, E64]. Furthermore, the Bull's focus on institutional stake increases since 2023 [E43, E44] ignores the current "NEGATIVE MONEY FLOW" [E45] and recent institutional outflows [E70]. The stock is explicitly flagged as "PRICE-LED," with price growth exceeding profit growth by 103%, indicating that market expectations are running dangerously ahead of actual delivery [E57, E58]. Conceded: the company is almost debt-free [E60] with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.02x [E38], yet borrowings have jumped from Rs 2 Cr to Rs 12 Cr in a single year [E40], and the stock carries extreme annualized volatility of 97.9% [E55]. Finally, the quarterly margin strength [E31] is undermined by an inconsistent trend over the last two quarters [E33] and a seasonally weak earnings profile in June [E59].

Conceded: long-term 5-year and 10-year compounded sales growth is 7% [E14, E15, E63], and the yearly and quarterly operating margin trends are officially labelled inconsistent [E32, E33]. However, dismissing the recent acceleration ignores a massive structural surge, including a 20% TTM sales growth [E17] and a quarterly sales jump of 31% year-over-year [E66]. Conceded: median ROE over the last three years is 10% [E28, E64], yet the business has decisively broken out to a 15.49% ROE and a 19.85% ROCE, both comfortably outperforming sector benchmarks of 10.35% and 11.68% [E9, E10]. Conceded: borrowings rose to Rs 12 Cr [E40], but the company remains virtually debt-free with a pristine 0.02x debt-to-equity ratio [E38, E60], backed by a robust Rs 156 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 118 Cr in free cash flow [E35, E36]. Conceded: annualized volatility reads 97.9% [E55], yet foreign and domestic institutional holdings have expanded since September 2023 [E43, E44], and the rules-based screen awards the setup a high-confidence 95 out of 100 [E65].

Conceded: the company delivered a TTM sales growth of 20% and a quarterly sales jump of 31% YoY [E17, E66], alongside a TTM operating margin increase to 20% [E30], but the long-term reality is a stagnant 5-year and 10-year compounded sales growth of just 7% [E14, E15, E63] with historical median ROE lingering at a low 5% to 10% over the last decade [E26, E27, E28, E64]. Conceded: the debt-to-equity ratio sits low at 0.02x [E38, E60], yet total borrowings spiked 500% from Rs 2 Cr to Rs 12 Cr [E40], and capital expenditure build-up is evident with CWIP jumping 96.2% to Rs 51 Cr [E41]. Conceded: foreign and domestic institutional stakes expanded compared to September 2023 [E43, E44], but recent institutional money flow has turned negative with a holding change of -0.19 percentage points [E45, E70]. Conceded: annualized volatility reaches an extreme 97.9% [E55] with a historical max drawdown of -95.5% [E54], and the stock price has dramatically outpaced fundamentals, recently growing faster than profit by 103% [E58] while trading at 3.22x book value [E2, E62].
